faqs.q: How is the freelance hourly rate calculated?
faqs.a: Pre-tax monthly need = (Income goal + Expenses) ÷ (1 − Tax%). Minimum rate = Pre-tax need ÷ Billable hours. Recommended is minimum × 1.3; premium is minimum × 1.6.
No. Every result is deterministic math from your inputs. There is no LLM, API call, or estimated “market rate”—only transparent formulas that update instantly.

faqs.q: What is the difference between minimum, recommended, and premium rates?
faqs.a: Minimum covers your goal and expenses after tax. Recommended adds a 30% buffer for unpaid work and risk. Premium (×1.6) positions you for specialized or high-demand work.

faqs.q: Who should use a freelance hourly rate calculator?
faqs.a: Freelancers, consultants, designers, developers, and agencies who need a clear floor rate before quoting clients or converting to project pricing.

faqs.q: Should I bill every hour at the recommended rate?
faqs.a: Use recommended as your target billable rate. Non-billable time (admin, sales, learning) is why the buffer exists—so your take-home still hits the goal.

faqs.q: Can I convert this hourly rate into a project price?
faqs.a: Yes. Pair this tool with Zetawala’s Freelance Project Pricing Calculator to fold in hours, revisions, and contingency into a fixed quote.
